body: 7 units · geology to population · drawn for a phone
This book is not “world geography” — it is **Eritrea**. Outcomes: read the land’s story (rocks), water, climate, plants and animals, soils, how people make a living, and who lives where.

f5.title: West → east vegetation sketch. Forests also store water, bind soil, and host wildlife.

cards.title: 4.1 Introduction to Vegetation and Wildlife
body: **Natural vegetation and wildlife** are the direct reflection of climate and relief.
Eritrea has a varied relief and climate.
When climate changes, the type of vegetation also changes.
**Eritrea** is a tropical country with physical diversity characterized by highlands and lowlands.
For example, along the coastlines and continental shelves, there are mangrove forests, sea grass and sea weeds.

cards.title: West → east vegetation sketch. Forests also store water, bind soil, and host wildlife.
From the coast to the plateau
body: **Coast:** mangroves, sea grass and sea weed; marine wildlife such as fish, dugongs and turtles.
**First 15–20 km inland:** widely spaced desert euphorbia and cactus. **Plains to the foot of the escarpment:** umbrella-shaped acacias; gazelle, wild ass, jackal and ostrich.

**Eastern escarpment:** olive and juniper, with leopard, bushbuck, klipspringer, greater kudu, duiker and warthog. **Plateau:** euphorbia and juniper. The sequence is controlled mainly by temperature, which falls with altitude.

options.B: variation in altitude, which changes temperature and rainfall

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Altitude ranges from below sea level in the Danakil to over 3,000 m at Emba Soira.

**Step 2:** Temperature falls and rainfall changes with altitude.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Natural vegetation of a region is mainly determined by:
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Plants need suitable temperature, water and nutrients.

**Step 2:** Rainfall and temperature decide which plants can grow (forest, savanna, desert); soil and relief modify this.

**Step 3:** Answer: climate and soil.

**Tip:** Wildlife distribution follows vegetation, because vegetation provides food and shelter.

cards.title: 4.2 Vegetation Cover in Eritrea
body: At the beginning of this century, the forest cover was estimated to be 30% of the total landmass of Eritrea.
According to a recent estimate by the Ministry of Agriculture, the forest cover has been reduced to about 0.4%.
Due to the great variation in altitude, climate, and topography, the vegetation cover of Eritrea shows great differences in terms of species diversity and cover.
In the past, the Highlands of Eritrea were covered by upland evergreen forest such as juniper and olive trees and montane evergreen forests.
Montane evergreen forests are forests that grow in the Highlands.

body: Forest cover fell from about 30% of the land early in the 20th century to 11% in 1952, 5% in 1960 and about 0.4% today.

cards.title: How fast the forests disappeared
body: Forest cover fell from about **30%** of Eritrea (around 1900) to **11%** (1952), **5%** (1960) and about **0.4%** today.

Three forest/woodland types: **highland forests** of juniper and olive on the plateau; **acacia woodland**, covering about a quarter of the country in the lowlands and lower escarpments; and **riverine forests** with doum palms along the Gash-Mereb, Setit and Barka, threatened by commercial farming.

All natural vegetation together (forest, shrubland and grassland) covers only about 33% of the land. The dense forest left (about 53,000 ha) is in the Green Belt and Rora Habab. About 10,000 ha are non-native eucalyptus.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Definitely soil erosion is **not** very active in places where

options.B: The land is dominant by sandy soil.
options.C: rainfall is abundant and with heavy storms.
options.D: the slope of the land is steep.
options.E: the slope of the land is gentle and associated with evergreen.

cards.why: Soil erosion is minimized when the **slope is gentle** (slower water runoff) and there is **vegetation cover** (evergreen), which protects the soil surface from the impact of rain and binds the soil with roots.

cards.title: Exam question, solved
cards.problem: Erosion is very active in place with:  A) Sand soil  B) Steep slope  C) No vegetation cover  D) Heavy rain fall  E) All

steps.text: **Step 1.** Soil erosion is accelerated by several factors: **Sand soil** is easily detached; **Steep slopes** increase the velocity of runoff; **Lack of vegetation** leaves soil unprotected; and **Heavy rainfall** provides the energy to wash away soil.
**Step 2.** Therefore, all factors contribute to active erosion.

**Step 2: Conclude**

cards.title: Quick check

**Step 1: Identify native highland conifers**
The native highland climax forests of Eritrea are composed of slow-growing conifers, specifically **Juniper (*Juniperus procera*)** and Wild Olive.

**Step 2: Compare other options**
* Eucalyptus: non-native/exotic.
* Doum Palm: riverine lowland.
* Mangrove: coastal intertidal.

**Step 3: Conclude**
The correct answer is Juniper.

cards.title: 4.3 Distribution of Natural Vegetation
body: Temperature decreases towards the Highlands while there is increase of rainfall.
The vegetation of the coastal plains of Eritrea is heterogeneous (diverse) in terms of both species diversity and distribution.
The vegetation here includes swamps along seasonal rivers and wadis, acacia woodland, semi desert acacia woodland, bush lands, desert scrubs and mangrove.
The shrubs are mainly 1 to 4 meters tall with scarce ground vegetation.
Mangroves are found along the coastal areas between the sea and the land.

cards.title: Vegetation belts from the coast to the western lowlands
body: **Coast and islands:** mangroves (evergreen trees up to about 6 m growing in shallow salt water, e.g. around Massawa, the Gulf of Zula and islands such as Norah and Dissei), sea grass and halophytes (salt-tolerant plants, some succulent).

**Sub-desert steppe** (up to about 200 m, within 15–20 km of the coast): widely spaced drought-resistant plants such as desert euphorbia. Massawa gets about 190 mm of rain but loses about 1,900 mm to evapotranspiration.
**True savanna / thorny steppe** (200–700 m, to the foot of the escarpment, 200–400 mm rain): dwarf grasses and umbrella-shaped acacias with small leaves that reduce transpiration.

**Eastern escarpment** (700–2,000 m, two rainy seasons): semi-arid woodland at the foot (euphorbia, aloe, baobab), semi-humid woodland (400–800 mm; olive, juniper, tamarind) and the **Green Belt** (800–1,300 mm) – dense, tall evergreen forest around Filfil, Solomuna and Mirara.

**Highlands** (1,500–3,000 m, 500–700 mm): upland dry evergreen forest of juniper and olive, now heavily deforested. **Western escarpment and lowlands:** deciduous open woodland, acacia bushland and wooded savanna; tall grassland south of the Barentu–Tesseney road, ideal for grazing, with doum palms.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which one of the following is **not true** about natural vegetation in Eritrea?

options.A: Mangrove forests are grown in the shallow coastal salty water.
options.B: Natural vegetation and wild life are the direct reflection of relief and climate of an area.
options.C: Acacia woodland occupy ¼ of the surface of Eritrea.
options.D: Forests have economic, recreational or Aesthetic and environmental values.
options.E: xerophytes are either succulent or hygroscopic plants.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Evaluate A, B, D.** These are standard geographic facts regarding mangroves, ecological relationships, and forest values.
**Step 2: Evaluate E.** Xerophytes (desert plants) are indeed succulent (store water) or have adaptations to survive drought.
**Step 3: Evaluate C.** Acacia woodland and shrubland actually occupy a much larger portion of Eritrea (estimated at over 60-70% of the land area), not just 1/4 (25%).
**Step 4: Conclusion.** C is the incorrect statement.

cards.title: 4.4.1 Importance of forests
body: Forests also have recreational and aesthetic values.
The natural beauty and peace in forests offer a special source of enjoyment.
Many people throughout the world, use forests for different activities such as camping, hiking and hunting.
Many people also visit forests simply to enjoy themselvesand relax in the quiet beauty of forests.

cards.title: 4.4.2 The Importance of Tree Planting as a Source of Development
body: If natural vegetation is wisely managed, it provides a continuous source of wood and many other wood products.
The trees add nutrients to the soil through nitrogen fixation.

cards.title: Why forests matter
body: **Economic:** timber, fuel wood, food, medicines, oils, gums and fibres. **Recreation and beauty:** walking, camping and relaxation.

**Environmental:** leaves break the force of rain; litter and humus absorb water, reduce runoff and flooding, and recharge groundwater. Trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen, and they keep the local climate milder and more humid.

**Agro-forestry** combines trees with crops or livestock, giving fuel, fruit, fodder and soil nitrogen. Planting trees creates rural jobs, uses land unsuitable for crops and protects soil from erosion.

cards.title: 4.5 Environmental Issues
body: The largest part of Eritrea, particularly the central highlands where there is dense population, have been deforested.
Overgrazing and rapid urbanization also led to deforestation to a considerable degree.
Wild animals have lost their habitat and fled to neighboring states or died.
To do so, contact community leaders parents, or resource people from the Ministry of Agriculture.

cards.title: Deforestation: causes and consequences
body: **Causes:** thirty years of war (bombing, trenches, buildings), clearing land for farming, felling trees for fuel and building, wood and charcoal concessions since the Italian period, recurrent drought, overgrazing and rapid urban growth.

**Consequences:** fuel shortages, so dung and crop residues are burned instead of returning to the soil; soil erosion and falling yields; more flooding, siltation of dams and desertification; drier soils; timber shortages; loss of wildlife habitat and endangered species.
**Responses:** tree planting, area closures (enclosures), terracing, fuel-saving stoves and protected areas.

cards.title: Step by step: Environmental issues in Eritrea
body: **Step 1:** Identify the problem: deforestation, soil erosion, land degradation, loss of wildlife and desertification.
**Step 2:** Causes: fuel-wood and charcoal use, clearing for farming, overgrazing, recurrent drought, the thirty-year war and rapid urban growth.
**Step 3:** Consequences: fuel shortages (dung and crop residues burned instead of returned to the soil), falling soil fertility, silting of dams, loss of habitats and wildlife.
**Step 4:** Solutions: afforestation and hillside closures, terracing and check dams, improved stoves and alternative energy, controlled grazing and protected areas.
**Step 5:** Community participation, environmental education and laws make the solutions last.
**Example:** Burning dung for cooking instead of using it as manure is a chain effect of deforestation: no trees → no fuel-wood → dung burned → less manure → lower crop yields.

cards.title: Wildlife in Eritrea
body: **Wildlife (book examples):** African wild ass (arid north & Red Sea regions — globally endangered, relatively better off in Eritrea), Nubian ibex, elephant remnants in Gash-Barka (Haikota, Augaro, Antore), greater kudu, gazelles, warthog, ostrich, plus marine life (dugong, turtle). Threats: habitat loss, hunting, drought. Response: protected areas and conservation programmes.

cards.title: Exam sticky notes
body: - Wild ass = globally endangered, better in ER

cards.title: 4.6.1 Introduction
body: In the equatorial climate, rainfall is daily and heavy, while temperature and relative humidity are high.
In the savanna grassland, rainfall is seasonal.
The region is dominated by abundant animals.

cards.title: 4.6.2 Present Situation of Wildlife in Eritrea
body: Eritrea exhibits a wide variety of natural ecosystems that are well-distributed across the country.

Historically, Eritrea had a wide range of animal species such as elephant, hippopotamus, buffalo, giraffe, greater kudu, wild ass, Nubian ibex, water buck, lion, leopard, cheetah, colobus monkey, and others.
At present, some of these species exist in parts of Eritrea, but their number is small and is under threat.

In general, the number of wild animal in Eritrea has decreased considerably due to hunting, war, deforestation of the animal habitat, drought, the growth of towns and villages and the development of roads.

glossary.meaning: Sub-Desert Steppe are the same as A. savanna.
Natural vegetation and wildlife are the direct reflection of climate and relief.
Eritrea is a tropical country with physical diversity characterized by highlands and lowlands.

tips.text: Its climate is influenced by its latitudinal position, but physical diversity is the most important factor that determines the climate of Eritrea.
The climate varies from desert in the eastern Lowlands to temperate climate in the Highlands.
The natural vegetation and wildlife of Eritrea is the direct reflection of the climate.
In general, there is relationship among climate, natural vegetation, and wildlife in Eritrea.
Because of human activities such as cutting trees for agricultural purpose, timber, and fuel, vegetation cover has been reduced greatly.
Around 100 years ago, about 30% of Eritrea’s total area was covered by forests, but this has been reduced to 0.41% at present.
The present types of forests are Highland vegetation, acacia woodland, and riverine forests. There are also grasslands in the Lowlands.

The natural vegetation in Eritrea are classified into natural vegetation of eastern Lowlands, natural vegetation of eastern Escarpment, temperate vegetation of the Highlands, natural vegetation of western Escarpment, and vegetation of western Lowlands.
There are different kinds of wild animals in Eritrea. However their number has been reduced greatly due to deforestation and prolonged war.
The distribution of these wild animals is also influenced by topography.
Exam sticky notes: - Wild ass = globally endangered, better in ER

questions.q: Which one of the following is **wrong** statement about monsoon forests?

options.B: They occupy lesser land area than selvas.
options.C: There have less number of species than selvas.
options.D: The trees are tall and widely spaced allowing under growth.
options.E: Rapid growth of trees during the wet season.

why: Statement A is wrong because trees in monsoon forests are **deciduous**, meaning they shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve water. Selvas (rainforests) are evergreen (non-deciduous).
